overview: The two vascular tissues in plants, transporting different materials in different directions.
genZNote: Xylem: one-way water delivery, straight up. Phloem: two-way food delivery, wherever it's needed.

aspects.label: Direction of Transport
aspects.valueA: Unidirectional — upward, from roots to leaves.
aspects.valueB: Bidirectional — can move food up or down, depending on where it's needed (source to sink).

aspects.label: State of Conducting Cells
aspects.valueA: Conducting cells (tracheids, vessels) are dead at maturity.
aspects.valueB: Conducting cells (sieve tubes) are living, though they lack a nucleus at maturity.

aspects.label: Mechanism of Movement
aspects.valueA: Passive movement driven by transpiration pull and root pressure.
aspects.valueB: Active process — pressure flow (mass flow) hypothesis, requiring energy.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Xylem transport is passive (driven by transpiration), while phloem transport requires ATP for active loading of sugars — a frequently tested contrast.
overlay.memoryTrick: Xylem = 'X' for 'eXit upward only', water. Phloem = flows both ways, food.
overlay.commonMisconception: Phloem is not one-directional like xylem — its transport direction depends on where sugars are being produced (source) versus used or stored (sink).
